chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

Dhahr (male's declaration to his wife that she is to him as the back of her mother) is of two types: in one of them there is an expiation, when he says, 'You are to me as the back of my mother,' and he does not say, 'You are to me as the back of my mother if I approach you,' and this does not contradict these narrations.

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Dhahr, a form of divorce where a husband declares his wife like the back of his mother
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation, the penalty required for certain acts including Dhahr

ai.seo_question: What are the different types of Dhahr and their respective legal rulings in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani clarifies the jurisprudential nuance that the declaration of Dhahr is only valid when accompanied by an oath (yamin), as indicated by the chapter title. It distinguishes between a simple declaration requiring expiation and a conditional one, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the precise wording of the oath in establishing the legal binding of the act.
